target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply imageMaxDimensionPx resize to image description input (#101923)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101923. The image description pre-processing pipeline (`prepareImageDescriptionInput`) passes images through at original dimensions without applying `agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx`. Phone-camera photos (typically 4000×8000) exceed provider limits and fail with:

```
Image dimensions exceed the 25,000,000 pixel input limit: 4536x8064
```

This affects `openclaw infer image describe --model ...`, `describeImageFileWithModel`, and `describePreparedImageWithModel`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a `resizeToJpeg` step after `normalizeImageDescriptionInput` when `imageMaxDimensionPx` is configured, reusing the same image-ops resize ladder already used by the tool image output sanitizer.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — resizeToJpeg with maxSide=2000

Generates a 3000×3000 BMP (27MB), passes through the exact `resizeToJpeg` function used in `prepareImageDescriptionInput`, and verifies the result respects the 2000px limit:

```
=== Before resize ===
Dimensions: 3000x3000 | bytes: 27000054

=== After resizeToJpeg(maxSide=2000) ===
Dimensions: 2000x2000 | bytes: 69717
Within 2000px limit: true

✅ imageMaxDimensionPx enforcement works
```

Run with: `node --import tsx/esm -e "import { resizeToJpeg, getImageMetadata } from './src/media/image-ops.ts'; ..."`

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/media-understanding/runtime.ts` | +14: `resizeToJpeg` with `maxSide` from `imageMaxDimensionPx` when configured in `prepareImageDescriptionInput` |
